charger.title: Charger - sensors

data_description.status_entity_id: Charger status (Supported states: on, connect, connected, ready, ready_to_charge, awaiting_authorization, awaiting_start, off, disconnect, disconnected, charging, completed, finished)

data_description.charging_phases: Number of phases the car charges with (1-3).

load_balancing.title: Load balancing
load_balancing.description: The place of the car in the shared grid connection.

data_description.site_priority: 1 = charges first. A car under the daily minimum or with a trip soon always goes first.

ev.title: EV - sensors (optional)
ev.description: Sensors from the car integration. Without a car integration leave them empty: a virtual battery level that you set is used instead. Battery level, range and odometer must either all be set or all be empty.

data_description.charge_port_door_entity_id: Indicates port open/closed (Supported states: on, open, plugged, connect, connected, plugged_waiting_for_charge, manual, off, closed, unplugged, disconnect, disconnected)
data_description.charge_cable_entity_id: Indicates if vehicle is connected (Supported states: on, open, plugged, connect, connected, plugged_waiting_for_charge, manual, off, closed, unplugged, disconnect, disconnected)
data_description.charging_limit_entity_id: Optional: the current charge limit of the car. Used for the charging loss calculation and rounding (Kia/Cupra). The wanted limit is published as the sensor charging_limit.
data_description.location_entity_id: If not set, falls back to charger.entity_ids.status_entity_id for home/away
data_description.last_update_entity_id: Optional: time of the last update of the car. No wake_up event when the car updated within 14 minutes.
data_description.climate_entity_id: Optional: the climate entity of the car. Its state tells if preheating runs; start/stop are fired as events on ev_request.

ev_specs.title: EV - battery
ev_specs.description: The battery of the car and how early charging must be done before departure.

data_description.battery_size: Usable battery capacity; verify via OBD2
data_description.last_charging_hour_before_departure_buff: Hours before departure when charging must be completed. If energy is missing, additional charging will be scheduled.

instance.title: Add EV / charger
instance.description: Cable Juice Planner plans when the EV should charge from electricity prices, driving, solar forecast and home battery. The integration sends no commands to the charger or the car: the plan and the actions are published as entities (e.g. `sensor.cjp_‹prefix›_charger_action` and the amps sensors) that you use in your own automations.

data_description.name: Optional, e.g. Tesla or Family car. Used as the device name (entities show as e.g. Tesla Overview) and in the notifications.
data_description.entity_prefix: Optional. All entities start with cjp_, the prefix follows: tesla gives sensor.cjp_tesla_overview, empty gives sensor.cjp_overview. Use a different prefix for each car. Cannot be changed later.
data_description.language: Language of the overview, the charging history, the charging rule and notifications.

site.title: Shared grid connection
site.description: Load balancing between several cars: the cars are planned by priority, so together they never use more current per phase than the main fuse. A car with lower priority charges with fewer amps or in other hours.

data_description.fuse_l1: The main fuse (or the limit the cars may use together) per phase.
data_description.fuse_l2: The main fuse (or the limit the cars may use together) per phase.
data_description.fuse_l3: The main fuse (or the limit the cars may use together) per phase.
data_description.margin: Subtracted from the fuse to leave room for short peaks.
data_description.voltage: Used when the phase sensors measure power (W) instead of current (A).
data_description.phase_l1_entity_id: Optional: measured current (A) or power (W) per phase of the whole house (e.g. a HAN/P1 meter). With all three the house consumption is subtracted and an overloaded phase limits the last car at once. Without them the fuse is a fixed budget for the cars.
data_description.phase_l2_entity_id: Optional: measured current (A) or power (W) per phase of the whole house (e.g. a HAN/P1 meter). With all three the house consumption is subtracted and an overloaded phase limits the last car at once. Without them the fuse is a fixed budget for the cars.
data_description.phase_l3_entity_id: Optional: measured current (A) or power (W) per phase of the whole house (e.g. a HAN/P1 meter). With all three the house consumption is subtracted and an overloaded phase limits the last car at once. Without them the fuse is a fixed budget for the cars.
data_description.urgent_trip_hours: A planned trip within this many hours gives the car precedence.

backup.description:
Export writes the databases, settings and configuration to a file in **cable_juice_planner_backups**.

Importing a file replaces the databases and settings of **{prefix}** with the backup (the current data is exported first, as a *_before_import* file) and reloads the integration.

data_description.restore_configuration: Use the entities and options of the backup as well. Leave off when the backup comes from another Home Assistant.

confirm.title: Update the blueprint {name}
confirm.description:
Cable Juice Planner comes with a version of the blueprint **{name}** that differs from `{path}`.

Select **Submit** to replace the file with the bundled version and reload the automations that use it. Changes you made to the file yourself are overwritten – copy it to another file name first if you want to keep them.

Ignore this repair to keep your own file.
